checks: Checked source 6a014eb26413a72b §1, (2) and 8095e181b6be7bf1 §4 against the frozen source hashes. The first gives the right derivative and the second the unperturbed one-zero cap value.

In the d positive-vertex coordinates the reference simplex has volume 1/d!. Scaling each coordinate by (b_j−ε)/(t−ε) yields the orthant-cap fraction. If t>y, scaling slightly inward from an axis intercept beyond sum u_j=1 and then perturbing into the orthant yields an open region of removed positive volume.

For positive ε the ratio decreases on (ε,y], the cap is zero at or below ε, and the ratio is t at and above M. Compactness on [y,M] gives a minimizer. Along any convergent sequence of minimizers, cap probabilities converge because the unperturbed affine form is nonconstant and has no atom at the limiting threshold. Comparing with the ratio at y and using strict clipping above y proves the limit is y.

The orthant bound gives the lower ratio at t_ε and equality at y gives the upper ratio there. The product term has relative derivative −Σ_j 1/(d b_j). Since t_ε→y>0, the lower ratio factor is 1+ε/y+o(ε), the same first-order term as at y. If y=M, all thresholds in the localization interval coincide and the derivative is zero, covering d=1.

As an independent check, when d=2 and b=(1,4), the top interval has F(t)=1−(4−t)^2/[3(4−ε)]. The unique minimizing threshold there is 1+3ε/4 and the value is √(4+3ε), whose right derivative 3/4 equals the displayed formula.
